name: Generation Alpha
description: Digital-native generation raised around tablets, streaming, AI-assisted tools, and highly connected media.

name: Baby Boomers
description: Post-war generation whose adulthood spans major economic, social, and technological changes.

name: Silent Generation
description: Pre-digital generation shaped by wartime/post-war society and traditional institutions.

name: Interwar Generation
description: Born between the World Wars and reaching adulthood around WWII.

name: Greatest Generation
description: Early-20th-century cohort whose adulthood was heavily shaped by depression and global war.

name: Lost Generation
description: Late-Victorian-born cohort associated historically with WWI-era adulthood and early modernity.

name: Progressive Generation
description: Mid-19th-century cohort useful for Victorian and industrial-era personas.

name: Missionary Generation
description: Late-19th-century cohort spanning industrialisation and major social change.

name: Gilded Generation
description: Early/mid-19th-century cohort useful for industrial and Victorian settings.

name: Romantic Generation
description: Napoleonic/early-industrial-era cohort useful for Regency and early Victorian contexts.

name: Revolutionary Generation
description: Enlightenment-era cohort reaching adulthood during major political revolutions.

name: Enlightenment Generation
description: Early-modern cohort useful for Enlightenment and pre-industrial characters.

name: Renaissance Cohort
description: Broad PersonaForge grouping for characters shaped by Renaissance-era societies.

name: Medieval Cohort
description: Broad historical cohort for medieval personas where modern generation labels aren't useful.

name: Ancient Cohort
description: Broad fallback for ancient historical settings rather than forcing modern generational concepts.

name: Rapid Digital Transition Cohort
description: People whose formative education or early working life moved abruptly from mostly offline institutions to networked, mobile, and automated systems.

name: Post-Conflict Rebuilding Cohort
description: People who came of age while communities repaired infrastructure, institutions, trust, and family networks after a major conflict.

name: Displaced Migrant Cohort
description: People whose formative years were shaped by forced movement, resettlement, divided identity, and adapting between cultural or linguistic systems.

name: Deindustrialised Cohort
description: People raised in communities where factories, mines, or major employers closed and families adapted to long-term economic restructuring.

name: Climate-Disrupted Cohort
description: People whose formative environment was repeatedly shaped by ecological disruption, resource limits, extreme weather, or climate adaptation.

name: Austerity-Raised Cohort
description: People who grew up amid prolonged public-service cuts, insecure work, constrained opportunity, and household resource management.

name: Frontier Settlement Cohort
description: People formed by life in a newly settled or expanding community where institutions, supply lines, laws, and social norms were still being built.
